his belt sailor fashion og med a shrug of oriental obeisance salutes
the court, pointing one thumb heavenward.)_ Him makee velly muchee fine
nat. _(He begins to lilt simply.)_

Li li poo lil chile
     Blingee pigfoot evly nat
     Payee two shilly...
_(He is howled down.)_

J. J. O’MOLLOY: _(Hotly til den populace.)_ This is a lonehand fight. By
Hades, jeg vil ikke have any client of mine gagged og badgered in this
fashion by a pack of curs og laughing hyenas. The Mosaic code has
superseded the law af den jungle. I say it og I say it emphatically,
without wishing for one moment to defeat the ends of justice, accused
var ikke accessory før the act og prosecutrix har ikke been tampered
med. The young person was treated by defendant as if she were his meget
own datter. _(Bloom takes J. J. O’Molloy’s hånd og raises it to his
lips.)_ I shall call rebutting evidence to prove up til den hilt that
the hidden hånd is igen at its gammel game. da in doubt persecute
Bloom. My client, an innately bashful mand, would be the last mand i den
verden to do noget som helst ungentlemanly which injured modesty could object
to eller cast a sten at a pige hvem took the wrong turning da nogle
dastard, responsible for her condition, had worked his own sweet will
on her. He wants to go straight. I regard him as the whitest mand I
know. He is down on his luck at present owing til den mortgaging of his
extensive property at Agendath Netaim in faraway Asia Minor, slides of
which will nu be shown. _(To Bloom.)_ I suggest that you will do the
handsome thing.
BLOOM: A penny i den pound.

_(The image af den lake of Kinnereth med blurred cattle cropping in
silver haze is projected på den wall. Moses Dlugacz, ferreteyed albino,
in blue dungarees, stands up i den gallery, holding in each hånd an
orange citron og a pork kidney.)_
DLUGACZ: _(Hoarsely.)_ Bleibtreustrasse, Berlin, W. 13.

_(J. J. O’Molloy steps on to a low plinth og holds the lapel of his
coat med solemnity. His ansigt lengthens, grows pale og bearded, med
sunken øjne, the blotches of phthisis og hectic cheekbones of John F.
Taylor. He applies his handkerchief to his mouth og scrutinises the
galloping tide of rosepink blood.)_

J. J. O’MOLLOY: _(Almost voicelessly.)_ Excuse me. jeg er suffering fra
a severe chill, have recently come fra a sickbed. A få wellchosen
words. _(He assumes the avine hoved, foxy moustache og proboscidal
eloquence of Seymour Bushe.)_ da the angel’s book comes to be opened
if aught that the pensive bosom has inaugurated of soultransfigured og
of soultransfiguring deserves to live I say accord the prisoner ved den
bar the sacred benefit af den doubt.
_(A paper med noget written on it is handed ind i court._)

BLOOM: _(In court dress.)_ Can give best references. Messrs Callan,
Coleman. Mr Wisdom Hely J. P. My gammel chief Joe Cuffe. Mr V. B. Dillon,
ex lord mayor of Dublin. jeg har moved i den charmed circle af den
highest... Queens of Dublin society. _(Carelessly.)_ jeg var bare
chatting this afternoon ved den viceregal lodge to my gammel pals, sir
Robert og lady Ball, astronomer royal, ved den levee. Sir Bob, I
said...

MRS YELVERTON BARRY: _(In lowcorsaged opal balldress og elbowlength
ivory gloves, wearing a sabletrimmed brickquilted dolman, a comb of
brilliants og panache of osprey in her hair.)_ Arrest him, constable.
He wrote me an anonymous letter in prentice backhand da my husband
was i den North Riding of Tipperary på den Munster circuit, signed
James Lovebirch. sagde han that han havde seen fra den gods my peerless
globes as I sat in a box af den _Theatre Royal_ at a command
performance of _La Cigale_. I deeply inflamed him, sagde han. han lavede
improper overtures to me to misconduct myself at half past four p.m. on
the following Thursday, Dunsink tid. He offered to send me gennem den
post a work of fiction by Monsieur Paul de Kock, entitled _The pige
med den Three Pairs of Stays_.

MRS BELLINGHAM: _(In cap og seal coney mantle, wrapped up til den nose,
steps ud of her brougham og scans through tortoiseshell
quizzing-glasses which she takes fra inside her huge opossum muff.)_
Also to me. ja, I believe it is the same objectionable person. Because
he closed my carriage dør outside sir Thornley Stoker’s one sleety dag
during the cold snap of February ninetythree da endda the grid af den
wastepipe og the ballstop in my bath cistern were frozen. Subsequently
he enclosed a bloom of edelweiss culled på den heights, as sagde han, in
my honour. jeg havde it examined by a botanical expert og elicited the
information that det var a blossom af den homegrown potato plant
purloined fra a forcingcase af den model farm.
MRS YELVERTON BARRY: Shame on him!
_(A crowd of sluts og ragamuffins surges forward.)_

THE SLUTS og RAGAMUFFINS: _(Screaming.)_ Stop thief! Hurrah der,
Bluebeard! Three cheers for Ikey Mo!
SECOND WATCH: _(Produces handcuffs.)_ her are the darbies.

MRS BELLINGHAM: He addressed me in several handwritings med fulsome
compliments as a Venus in furs og alleged profound pity for my
frostbound coachman Palmer while i den same breath he expressed
himself as envious of his earflaps og fleecy sheepskins og of his
fortunate proximity to my person, da standing behind my chair wearing
my livery og the armorial bearings af den Bellingham escutcheon
garnished sable, a buck’s hoved couped eller. He lauded almost
extravagantly my nether extremities, my swelling calves in silk hose
drawn up til den limit, og eulogised glowingly my other hidden
treasures in priceless lace which, sagde han, han kunne conjure up. He
urged me (Stating that han følte it his mission in liv to urge me.) to
defile the marriage bed, to commit adultery ved den earliest possible
opportunity.

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: _(In amazon costume, hard hat,
jackboots cockspurred, vermilion waistcoat, fawn musketeer gauntlets
med braided drums, lang train held up og hunting crop med which she
strikes her welt constantly.)_ Also me. Because han så me på den polo
ground af den Phoenix park ved den match alle Ireland versus the Rest of
Ireland. My øjne, jeg ved, shone divinely as I watched Captain Slogger
Dennehy af den Inniskillings win the final chukkar on his darling cob
_Centaur._ This plebeian Don Juan observed me fra behind a hackney car
og sent me in double envelopes an obscene photograph, such as are sold
efter mørk on Paris boulevards, insulting to any lady. jeg har it stadig.
It represents a partially nude señorita, frail og lovely (his wife, as
he solemnly assured me, taken by him fra nature), practising illicit
intercourse med a muscular torero, evidently a blackguard. He urged me
to do likewise, to misbehave, to sin med officers af den garrison. He
implored me to soil his letter in an unspeakable manner, to chastise
him as he richly deserves, to bestride og ride him, to give him a mest
vicious horsewhipping.
MRS BELLINGHAM: Me også.
MRS YELVERTON BARRY: Me også.

_(Several highly respectable Dublin ladies hold up improper letters
received fra Bloom.)_

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: _(Stamps her jingling spurs in a
sudden paroxysm of fury.)_ jeg vil, ved den gud above me. I’ll scourge
the pigeonlivered cur as lang as I can stand over him. I’ll flay him
alive.

BLOOM: _(His øjne closing, quails expectantly.)_ her? _(He squirms.)_
igen! _(He pants cringing.)_ I kærlighed the danger.

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: meget meget so! I’ll make it hot for
you. I’ll make you dance Jack Latten for that.

MRS BELLINGHAM: Tan his breech well, the upstart! Write the stjerner og
stripes on it!

MRS YELVERTON BARRY: Disgraceful! der’s nej excuse for him! A married
mand!

BLOOM: alle these people. I meant kun the spanking idea. A warm
tingling glow without effusion. Refined birching to stimulate the
circulation.

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: _(Laughs derisively.)_ O, did you,
my fine fellow? Well, ved den living gud, you’ll get the surprise of
your liv nu, believe me, the mest unmerciful hiding a mand ever
bargained for. You have lashed the dormant tigress in my nature ind i
fury.

MRS BELLINGHAM: _(Shakes her muff og quizzing-glasses vindictively.)_
Make him smart, Hanna dear. Give him ginger. Thrash the mongrel within
an inch of his liv. The cat-o’-nine-tails. Geld him. Vivisect him.

BLOOM: _(Shuddering, shrinking, joins his hands: med hangdog mien.)_ O
cold! O shivery! det var your ambrosial beauty. Forget, forgive. Kismet.
Let me off this once. _(He offers the other cheek.)_

MRS YELVERTON BARRY: _(Severely.)_ Don’t do so on any account, Mrs
Talboys! He should be soundly trounced!

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: _(Unbuttoning her gauntlet
violently.)_ I’ll do nej such thing. Pigdog og altid was ever since he
was pupped! To dare address me! I’ll flog him black og blue i den
public streets. I’ll dig my spurs in him up til den rowel. He is a
wellknown cuckold. _(She swishes her huntingcrop savagely i den air.)_
Take down his trousers without loss of tid. Come her, sir! Quick!
Ready?
BLOOM: _(Trembling, beginning to obey.)_ The weather has been so warm.
_(Davy Stephens, ringletted, passes med a bevy of barefoot newsboys.)_

DAVY STEPHENS: _Messenger af den Sacred Heart_ og _Evening Telegraph_
med Saint Patrick’s dag supplement. Containing the ny addresses of
alle the cuckolds in Dublin.

_(The meget reverend Canon O’Hanlon in cloth of gold cope elevates og
exposes a marble timepiece. før him far Conroy og the reverend
John Hughes S. J. bend low.)_
THE TIMEPIECE: _(Unportalling.)_

Cuckoo.
     Cuckoo.
     Cuckoo.
_(The brass quoits of a bed are heard to jingle.)_
THE QUOITS: Jigjag. Jigajiga. Jigjag.

_(A panel of fog rolls back rapidly, revealing rapidly i den jurybox
the faces of Martin Cunningham, foreman, silkhatted, Jack Power, Simon
Dedalus, Tom Kernan, Ned Lambert, John Henry Menton, Myles Crawford,
Lenehan, Paddy Leonard, Nosey Flynn, M’Coy og the featureless ansigt of
a Nameless One.)_

THE NAMELESS ONE: Bareback riding. Weight for age. Gob, he organised
her.
THE JURORS: _(alle their heads turned to his stemme.)_ virkelig?
THE NAMELESS ONE: _(Snarls.)_ Arse over tip. Hundred shillings to five.

THE JURORS: _(alle their heads lowered in assent.)_ mest of us thought
as meget.

FIRST WATCH: He is a marked mand. Another pige’s plait cut. Wanted: Jack
the Ripper. A thousand pounds reward.
SECOND WATCH: _(Awed, whispers.)_ og in black. A mormon. Anarchist.

THE CRIER: _(Loudly.)_ Whereas Leopold Bloom of nej fixed abode is a
wellknown dynamitard, forger, bigamist, bawd og cuckold og a public
nuisance til den citizens of Dublin og whereas at this commission of
assizes the mest honourable...

_(His Honour, sir Frederick Falkiner, recorder of Dublin, in judicial
garb of grey sten rises fra den bench, stonebearded. He bears in his
arms an umbrella sceptre. fra his forehead arise starkly the Mosaic
ramshorns.)_

THE RECORDER: jeg vil put an end to this white slave traffic og rid
Dublin of this odious pest. Scandalous! _(He dons the black cap.)_ Let
him be taken, Mr Subsheriff, fra den dock hvor he nu stands og
detained in custody in Mountjoy prison during His Majesty’s pleasure
og der be hanged ved den neck until he is dead og therein fail ikke
at your peril eller may the Lord have mercy on your sjæl. Remove him. _(A
black skullcap descends upon his hoved.)_

_(The subsheriff lang John Fanning appears, smoking a pungent Henry
Clay.)_

lang JOHN FANNING: _(Scowls og calls med rich rolling utterance.)_
hvem’ll hang Judas Iscariot?

_(H. Rumbold, master barber, in a bloodcoloured jerkin og tanner’s
apron, a rope coiled over his shoulder, mounts the block. A liv
preserver og a nailstudded bludgeon are stuck in his belt. He rubs
grimly his grappling hands, knobbed med knuckledusters.)_

RUMBOLD: _(til den recorder med sinister familiarity.)_ Hanging Harry,
your Majesty, the Mersey terror. Five guineas a jugular. Neck eller
ingenting.
_(The bells of George’s church toll slowly, loud mørk iron.)_
THE BELLS: Heigho! Heigho!

BLOOM: _(Desperately.)_ Wait. Stop. Gulls. gud hjerte. jeg så.
Innocence. pige i den monkeyhouse. Zoo. Lewd chimpanzee.
_(Breathlessly.)_ Pelvic basin. Her artless blush unmanned me.
_(Overcome med emotion.)_ I left the precincts. (He turns to a figure
i den crowd, appealing.) Hynes, may I speak to you? You know me. That
three shillings you can keep. If you want a lille mere...
HYNES: _(Coldly.)_ You are a perfect stranger.
SECOND WATCH: _(Points til den corner.)_ The bomb is her.
FIRST WATCH: Infernal machine med a tid fuse.
BLOOM: nej, nej. Pig’s feet. jeg var at a funeral.
FIRST WATCH: _(Draws his truncheon.)_ Liar!

_(The beagle lifts his snout, showing the grey scorbutic ansigt of Paddy
Dignam. He has gnawed alle. He exhales a putrid carcasefed breath. He
grows to human size og shape. His dachshund coat becomes a brown
mortuary habit. His green øje flashes bloodshot. Half of one ear, alle
the nose og both thumbs are ghouleaten.)_

PADDY DIGNAM: _(In a hollow stemme.)_ It is sandt. det var my funeral.
Doctor Finucane pronounced liv extinct da I succumbed til den disease
fra natural causes.
_(He lifts his mutilated ashen ansigt moonwards og bays lugubriously.)_
BLOOM: _(In triumph.)_ You hear?
PADDY DIGNAM: Bloom, jeg er Paddy Dignam’s spirit. List, list, O list!
BLOOM: The stemme is the stemme of Esau.
SECOND WATCH: _(Blesses himself.)_ hvordan is that possible?
FIRST WATCH: It er ikke i den penny catechism.
PADDY DIGNAM: By metempsychosis. Spooks.
A stemme: O rocks.

PADDY DIGNAM: _(Earnestly.)_ Once jeg var i den employ of Mr J. H.
Menton, solicitor, commissioner for oaths og affidavits, of 27
Bachelor’s Walk. nu jeg er defunct, the wall af den hjerte hypertrophied.
Hard lines. The poor wife was awfully cut up. hvordan is she bearing it?
Keep her off that bottle of sherry. _(He looks round him.)_ A lamp. I
must satisfy an animal need. That buttermilk didn’t agree med me.

_(The portly figure of John O’Connell, caretaker, stands forth, holding
a bunch of keys tied med crape. Beside him stands far Coffey,
chaplain, toadbellied, wrynecked, in a surplice og bandanna nightcap,
holding sleepily a staff of twisted poppies.)_

far COFFEY: _(Yawns, så chants med a hoarse croak.)_ Namine.
Jacobs. Vobiscuits. Amen.

JOHN O’CONNELL: _(Foghorns stormily through his megaphone.)_ Dignam,
Patrick T, deceased.

PADDY DIGNAM: _(med pricked up ears, winces.)_ Overtones. _(He
wriggles forward og places an ear til den ground.)_ My master’s stemme!

JOHN O’CONNELL: Burial docket letter number U. P. eightyfive thousand.
Field seventeen. hus of Keys. Plot, one hundred og one.

_(Paddy Dignam listens med visible effort, thinking, his tail
stiffpointed, his ears cocked.)_
PADDY DIGNAM: Pray for the repose of his sjæl.

_(He worms down through a coalhole, his brown habit trailing its tether
over rattling pebbles. efter him toddles an obese grandfather rat on
fungus turtle paws under a grey carapace. Dignam’s stemme, muffled, is
heard baying under ground:_ Dignam’s dead og gone below. _Tom
Rochford, robinredbreasted, in cap og breeches, jumps fra his
twocolumned machine.)_

TOM ROCHFORD: _(A hånd to his breastbone, bows.)_ Reuben J. A florin I
find him. _(He fixes the manhole med a resolute stare.)_ My turn nu
on. Follow me up to Carlow.

_(He executes a daredevil salmon leap i den air og is engulfed i den
coalhole. Two discs på den columns wobble, øjne of nought. alle recedes.
Bloom plodges forward igen gennem den sump. Kisses chirp amid the
rifts of fog. A piano sounds. He stands før a lighted hus,
listening. The kisses, winging fra their bowers, fly om him,
twittering, warbling, cooing.)_

THE KISSES: _(Warbling.)_ Leo! _(Twittering.)_ Icky licky micky sticky
for Leo! _(Cooing.)_ Coo coocoo! Yummyyum, Womwom! _(Warbling.)_ stor
comebig! Pirouette! Leopopold! _(Twittering.)_ Leeolee! _(Warbling.)_ O
Leo!

_(They rustle, flutter upon his garments, alight, bright giddy flecks,
silvery sequins.)_
BLOOM: A mand’s touch. Sad musik. Church musik. måske her.

_(Zoe Higgins, a young whore in a sapphire slip, closed med three
bronze buckles, a slim black velvet fillet round her throat, nods,
trips down the steps og accosts him.)_
ZOE: Are you looking for someone? He’s inside med his ven.
BLOOM: Is this Mrs Mack’s?

ZOE: nej, eightyone. Mrs Cohen’s. You might go farther og fare worse.
mor Slipperslapper. _(Familiarly.)_ She’s på den job herself tonight
med den vet her tipster that gives her alle the winners og pays for
her søn in Oxford. Working overtime men her luck’s turned today.
_(Suspiciously.)_ You’re ikke his far, are you?
BLOOM: ikke I!
ZOE: You both in black. Has lille mousey any tickles tonight?

_(His skin, alert, feels her fingertips approach. A hånd glides over
his left thigh.)_
ZOE: hvordan’s the nuts?

BLOOM: Off side. Curiously they are på den right. Heavier, I suppose.
One in a million my tailor, Mesias, says.
ZOE: _(In sudden alarm.)_ You’ve a hard chancre.
BLOOM: ikke likely.
ZOE: I feel it.

_(Her hånd slides ind i his left trouser pocket og brings ud a hard
black shrivelled potato. She regards it og Bloom med dumb moist
lips.)_
BLOOM: A talisman. Heirloom.
ZOE: For Zoe? For keeps? For being so nice, eh?

_(She puts the potato greedily ind i a pocket så links his arm,
cuddling him med supple warmth. He smiles uneasily. Slowly, note by
note, oriental musik is played. He gazes i den tawny crystal of her
øjne, ringed med kohol. His smile softens.)_
ZOE: You’ll know me the next tid.

BLOOM: _(Forlornly.)_ I aldrig loved a dear gazelle men det var sure
to...

_(Gazelles are leaping, feeding på den mountains. Near are lakes. Round
their shores file shadows black of cedargroves. Aroma rises, a strong
hairgrowth of resin. It burns, the orient, a himmel of sapphire, cleft by
the bronze flight of eagles. under it lies the womancity, nude, white,
stadig, cool, in luxury. A fountain murmurs among damask roses. Mammoth
roses murmur of scarlet winegrapes. A wine of shame, lust, blood
exudes, strangely murmuring.)_

ZOE: _(Murmuring singsong med den musik, her odalisk lips lusciously
smeared med salve of swinefat og rosewater.) Schorach ani wenowach,
benoith Hierushaloim._
BLOOM: _(Fascinated.)_ I thought you were of gud stock by your accent.
ZOE: og you know hvad thought did?

_(She bites his ear gently med lille goldstopped teeth, sending on
him a cloying breath of stale garlic. The roses draw apart, disclose a
sepulchre af den gold of kings og their mouldering bones.)_

BLOOM: _(Draws back, mechanically caressing her right bub med a flat
awkward hånd.)_ Are you a Dublin pige?

ZOE: _(Catches a stray hair deftly og twists it to her coil.)_ nej
bloody fear. I’m English. Have you a swaggerroot?

BLOOM: _(As før.)_ Rarely smoke, dear. Cigar nu og så. Childish
device. _(Lewdly.)_ The mouth can be better engaged than med a
cylinder of rank weed.
ZOE: Go on. Make a stump speech ud of it.

BLOOM: _(In workman’s corduroy overalls, black gansy med red floating
tie og apache cap.)_ Mankind is incorrigible. Sir Walter Ralegh
brought fra den ny verden that potato og that weed, the one a killer
of pestilence by absorption, the other a poisoner af den ear, øje,
hjerte, memory, will, understanding, alle. That is to say he brought the
poison a hundred years før another person whose name I forget
brought the food. Suicide. Lies. alle our habits. hvorfor, look at our
public liv!
_(Midnight chimes fra distant steeples.)_
THE CHIMES: Turn igen, Leopold! Lord mayor of Dublin!

BLOOM: _(In alderman’s gown og chain.)_ Electors of Arran Quay, Inns
Quay, Rotunda, Mountjoy og North Dock, better run a tramline, I say,
fra den cattlemarket til den river. That’s the musik af den future.
That’s my programme. _Cui bono?_ men our bucaneering Vanderdeckens in
their phantom ship of finance...
AN ELECTOR: Three times three for our future chief magistrate!
_(The aurora borealis af den torchlight procession leaps.)_
THE TORCHBEARERS: Hooray!

_(Several wellknown burgesses, city magnates og freemen af den city
shake hands med Bloom og congratulate him. Timothy Harrington, late
thrice Lord Mayor of Dublin, imposing in mayoral scarlet, gold chain
og white silk tie, confers med councillor Lorcan Sherlock,_ locum
tenens. _They nod vigorously in agreement.)_

LATE LORD MAYOR HARRINGTON: _(In scarlet robe med mace, gold mayoral
chain og large white silk scarf.)_ That alderman sir Leo Bloom’s
speech be printed ved den expense af den ratepayers. That the hus in
which han var born be ornamented med a commemorative tablet og that
the thoroughfare hitherto known as Cow Parlour off Cork gade be
henceforth designated Boulevard Bloom.
COUNCILLOR LORCAN SHERLOCK: Carried unanimously.

BLOOM: _(Impassionedly.)_ These flying Dutchmen eller lying Dutchmen as
they recline in their upholstered poop, casting dice, hvad reck they?
Machines is their cry, their chimera, their panacea. Laboursaving
apparatuses, supplanters, bugbears, manufactured monsters for mutual
murder, hideous hobgoblins produced by a horde of capitalistic lusts
upon our prostituted labour. The poor mand starves while they are
grassing their royal mountain stags eller shooting peasants og
phartridges in their purblind pomp of pelf og power. men their reign
is rover for rever og ever og ev...

BLOOM: My subjects! We hereby nominate our faithful charger Copula

JOHN HOWARD PARNELL: _(Raises the royal standard.)_ Illustrious Bloom!
Successor to my famous bror!

BLOOM: _(Embraces John Howard Parnell.)_ We thank you fra our hjerte,

TOM KERNAN: You deserve it, your honour.

BLOOM: On this dag twenty years ago we overcame the hereditary enemy at

THE CHAPEL OF FREEMAN TYPESETTERS: Hear! Hear!
JOHN WYSE NOLAN: der’s the mand that got away James Stephens.
A BLUECOAT SCHOOLBOY: Bravo!

AN gammel RESIDENT: You’re a credit to your country, sir, that’s hvad you

AN APPLEWOMAN: He’s a mand som Ireland wants.

BLOOM: My beloved subjects, a ny era is om to dawn. I, Bloom, tell

THE SIGHTSEERS: _(Dying.) Morituri te salutant. (They die.)_

BLOOM: Shoot him! Dog of a christian! So meget for M’Intosh!

DR MULLIGAN: _(In motor jerkin, green motorgoggles on his brow.)_ Dr

elephantiasis have been discovered among his ascendants. der are
marked symptoms of chronic exhibitionism. Ambidexterity is also latent.
He is prematurely bald fra selfabuse, perversely idealistic in
consequence, a reformed rake, og has metal teeth. In consequence of a
family complex he has temporarily lost his memory og I believe him to
be mere sinned against than sinning. jeg har made a pervaginal
examination og, efter application af den acid test to 5427 anal,
axillary, pectoral og pubic hairs, I declare him to be _virgo
intacta._

DR CROTTHERS: jeg har examined the patient’s urine. It is albuminoid.

mange have found him a dear mand, a dear person. He is a rather quaint

court missionary af den Reformed Priests’ Protection Society which
clears up alt. He is practically a total abstainer og I can
affirm that he sleeps on a straw litter og eats the mest Spartan food,
cold dried grocer’s peas. He wears a hairshirt of pure Irish
manufacture winter og summer og scourges himself hver Saturday. He
was, I understand, at one tid a firstclass misdemeanant in Glencree

I appeal for clemency i den name af den mest sacred word our vocal
organs have ever been called upon to speak. He is om to have a baby.

wigged, singed, perfumesprayed, ricepowdered, med smoothshaven
armpits. Tape measurements will be taken next your skin. You will be
laced med cruel force ind i vicelike corsets of soft dove coutille med
whalebone busk til den diamondtrimmed pelvis, the absolute outside edge,
while your figure, plumper than da at large, will be restrained in
nettight frocks, pretty two ounce petticoats og fringes og things
stamped, of course, med my houseflag, creations of lovely lingerie for
Alice og nice scent for Alice. Alice will feel the pullpull. Martha
og Mary will be a lille chilly at first in such delicate thighcasing
men the frilly flimsiness of lace round your bare knees will remind
you...

BLOOM: _(A charming soubrette med dauby cheeks, mustard hair og large
male hands og nose, leering mouth.)_ I tried her things on kun twice,
a small prank, in Holles gade. da we were hard up I washed them to
save the laundry bill. My own shirts I turned. det var the purest
thrift.

BELLO: _(Jeers.)_ lille jobs that make mor pleased, eh? og showed
off coquettishly in your domino ved den mirror behind closedrawn blinds
your unskirted thighs og hegoat’s udders in various poses of
surrender, eh? Ho! ho! jeg har to laugh! That secondhand black operatop
shift og short trunkleg naughties alle split up the stitches at her
last rape that Mrs Miriam Dandrade sold you fra den Shelbourne hotel,
eh?
BLOOM: Miriam. Black. Demimondaine.

BELLO: _(Guffaws.)_ Christ Almighty it’s også tickling, this! You were a
nicelooking Miriam da you clipped off your backgate hairs og lay
swooning i den thing across the bed as Mrs Dandrade om to be
violated by lieutenant Smythe-Smythe, Mr Philip Augustus Blockwell M.
P., signor Laci Daremo, the robust tenor, blueeyed Bert, the liftboy,
Henri Fleury of Gordon Bennett fame, Sheridan, the quadroon Croesus,
the varsity wetbob eight fra gammel Trinity, Ponto, her splendid
Newfoundland og Bobs, dowager duchess of Manorhamilton. _(He guffaws
igen.)_ Christ, wouldn’t it make a Siamese cat laugh?

BLOOM: _(Her hands og features working.)_ det var Gerald converted me
to be a sandt corsetlover da jeg var female impersonator i den High
School play _Vice Versa_. det var dear Gerald. han fik that kink,
fascinated by søster’s stays. nu dearest Gerald uses pinky greasepaint
og gilds his eyelids. Cult af den beautiful.

BELLO: _(med wicked glee.)_ Beautiful! Give us a breather! da you
took your seat med womanish care, lifting your billowy flounces, on
the smoothworn throne.

BLOOM: Science. To compare the various joys we each enjoy.
_(Earnestly.)_ og virkelig it’s better the position... because ofte I
used to wet...

BELLO: _(Sternly.)_ nej insubordination! The sawdust is der i den
corner for you. I gave you strict instructions, didn’t I? Do it
standing, sir! I’ll teach you to behave som a jinkleman! If I catch a
trace on your swaddles. Aha! ved den ass af den Dorans you’ll find I’m a
martinet. The sins of your past are rising against you. mange. Hundreds.

THE SINS af den PAST: _(In a medley of voices.)_ han gik through a form
of clandestine marriage med at least one kvinde i den shadow af den
Black church. Unspeakable messages he telephoned mentally to Miss Dunn
at an address in D’Olier gade while he presented himself indecently
til den instrument i den callbox. By word og deed he frankly
encouraged a nocturnal strumpet to deposit fecal og other matter in an
unsanitary outhouse attached to empty premises. In five public
conveniences he wrote pencilled messages offering his nuptial partner
to alle strongmembered males. og ved den offensively smelling vitriol
works did he ikke pass nat efter nat by loving courting couples to
see if og hvad og hvordan meget han kunne see? Did he ikke lie in bed, the
gross boar, gloating over a nauseous fragment of wellused toilet paper
presented to him by a nasty harlot, stimulated by gingerbread og a
postal order?

BELLO: _(Whistles loudly.)_ Say! hvad was the mest revolting piece of
obscenity in alle your career of crime? Go the whole hog. Puke it ud!
Be candid for once.

_(Mute inhuman faces throng forward, leering, vanishing, gibbering,
Booloohoom. Poldy Kock, Bootlaces a penny, Cassidy’s hag, blind
stripling, Larry Rhinoceros, the pige, the kvinde, the whore, the other,

BLOOM: Don’t ask me! Our mutual faith. Pleasants gade. I kun thought
the half af den... I swear on my sacred oath...

BELLO: _(Peremptorily.)_ Answer. Repugnant wretch! I insist on knowing.
Tell me noget to amuse me, smut eller a bloody gud ghoststory eller a

mange? I give you bare three seconds. One! Two! Thr...
BLOOM: _(Docile, gurgles.)_ I rererepugnosed in rerererepugnant...

BELLO: _(Imperiously.)_ O, get ud, you skunk! Hold your tongue! Speak
da you’re spoken to.
BLOOM: _(Bows.)_ Master! Mistress! Mantamer!
_(He lifts his arms. His bangle bracelets fall.)_

BELLO: _(Satirically.)_ By dag you will souse og bat our smelling
underclothes also da we ladies are unwell, og swab ud our latrines
med dress pinned up og a dishclout tied to your tail. Won’t that be
nice? _(He places a ruby ring on her finger.)_ og der nu! med this
ring I thee own. Say, thank you, mistress.
BLOOM: Thank you, mistress.

BELLO: You will make the beds, get my tub ready, empty the pisspots in
the different rooms, including gammel Mrs Keogh’s the cook’s, a sandy one.
Ay, og rinse the seven of them well, sind, eller lap it up som
champagne. Drink me piping hot. Hop! You will dance attendance eller I’ll
lecture you on your misdeeds, Miss Ruby, og spank your bare bot right
well, miss, med den hairbrush. You’ll be taught the error of your
ways. At nat your wellcreamed braceletted hands will wear
fortythreebutton gloves newpowdered med talc og having delicately
scented fingertips. For such favours knights of gammel laid down their
lives. _(He chuckles.)_ My boys will be nej end charmed to see you so
ladylike, the colonel, above alle, da they come her the nat før
the wedding to fondle my ny attraction in gilded heels. First I’ll
have a go at you myself. A mand jeg ved på den turf named Charles Alberta
Marsh (jeg var in bed med him bare nu og another gentleman ud af den
Hanaper og Petty Bag office) is på den lookout for a maid of alle work
at a short knock. Swell the bust. Smile. Droop shoulders. hvad offers?
_(He points.)_ For that lot. Trained by owner to fetch og carry,
basket in mouth. _(He bares his arm og plunges it elbowdeep in Bloom’s
vulva.)_ der’s fine depth for you! hvad, boys? That give you a
hardon? _(He shoves his arm in a bidder’s ansigt.)_ her wet the deck og
wipe it round!
A BIDDER: A florin.
_(Dillon’s lacquey rings his handbell.)_
THE LACQUEY: Barang!
A stemme: One og eightpence også meget.
CHARLES ALBERTA MARSH: Must be virgin. gud breath. Clean.

BELLO: _(Gives a rap med his gavel.)_ Two bar. Rockbottom figure og
cheap ved den price. Fourteen hands high. Touch og examine shis points.
Handle hrim. This downy skin, these soft muscles, this tender flesh. If
jeg havde kun my gold piercer her! og quite easy to milk. Three newlaid
gallons a dag. A pure stockgetter, due to lay within the hour. His
sire’s milk record was a thousand gallons of whole milk in forty weeks.
Whoa, my jewel! Beg up! Whoa! _(He brands his initial C on Bloom’s
croup.)_ So! Warranted Cohen! hvad advance on two bob, gentlemen?
A DARKVISAGED mand: _(In disguised accent.)_ Hoondert punt sterlink.
VOICES: _(Subdued.)_ For the Caliph. Haroun Al Raschid.

BELLO: _(Gaily.)_ Right. Let them alle come. The scanty, daringly short
skirt, riding up ved den knee to show a peep of white pantalette, is a
potent weapon og transparent stockings, emeraldgartered, med den lang
straight seam trailing up beyond the knee, appeal til den better
instincts af den _blasé_ mand om town. Learn the smooth mincing walk
on four inch Louis Quinze heels, the Grecian bend med provoking croup,
the thighs fluescent, knees modestly kissing. Bring alle your powers of
fascination to bear on them. Pander to their Gomorrahan vices.

BLOOM: _(Bends his blushing ansigt ind i his armpit og simpers med
forefinger in mouth.)_ O, jeg ved hvad you’re hinting at nu!

BELLO: hvad else are you gud for, an impotent thing som you? _(He
stoops og, peering, pokes med his fan rudely under the fat suet folds
of Bloom’s haunches.)_ Up! Up! Manx cat! hvad have we her? hvor’s
your curly teapot gone to eller hvem docked it on you, cockyolly? Sing,
birdy, sing. It’s as limp as a dreng of six’s doing his pooly behind a
cart. Buy a bucket eller sell your pump. _(Loudly.)_ Can you do a mand’s
job?
BLOOM: Eccles gade...

BELLO: _(Sarcastically.)_ I wouldn’t hurt your feelings for the verden
men der’s a mand of brawn in possession der. The tables are turned,
my gay young fellow! He is noget som a fullgrown outdoor mand. Well
for you, you muff, if you had that weapon med knobs og lumps og
warts alle over it. He shot his bolt, I can tell you! Foot to foot, knee
to knee, belly to belly, bubs to breast! He’s nej eunuch. A shock of red
hair he has sticking ud of him behind som a furzebush! Wait for nine
months, my lad! Holy ginger, it’s kicking og coughing up og down in
her guts allerede! That makes you wild, don’t it? Touches the spot? _(He
spits in contempt.)_ Spittoon!

BLOOM: jeg var indecently treated, I... Inform the police. Hundred
pounds. Unmentionable. I...

BELLO: Would if you could, lame duck. A downpour we want ikke your
drizzle.
BLOOM: To drive me mad! Moll! I forgot! Forgive! Moll... We... stadig...

BELLO: _(Ruthlessly.)_ nej, Leopold Bloom, alle is changed by kvinde’s
will since you slept horizontal in Sleepy Hollow your nat of twenty
years. Return og see.
_(gammel Sleepy Hollow calls over the wold.)_
SLEEPY HOLLOW: Rip van Wink! Rip van Winkle!

BLOOM: _(In tattered mocassins med a rusty fowlingpiece, tiptoeing,
fingertipping, his haggard bony bearded ansigt peering gennem den
diamond panes, cries ud.)_ jeg ser her! It’s she! The first nat at Mat
Dillon’s! men that dress, the green! og her hair is dyed gold og
he...

BELLO: _(Laughs mockingly.)_ That’s your datter, you owl, med a
Mullingar student.

_(Milly Bloom, fairhaired, greenvested, slimsandalled, her blue scarf
i den seawind simply swirling, breaks fra den arms of her lover og
calls, her young øjne wonderwide.)_
MILLY: My! It’s Papli! men, O Papli, hvordan gammel you’ve grown!

BELLO: Changed, eh? Our whatnot, our writingtable hvor we aldrig wrote,
aunt Hegarty’s armchair, our classic reprints of gammel masters. A mand og
his menfriends are living der in clover. The _Cuckoos’ Rest!_ hvorfor
ikke? hvordan mange women had you, eh, following them up mørk streets,
flatfoot, exciting them by your smothered grunts, hvad, you male
prostitute? Blameless dames med parcels of groceries. Turn om.
Sauce for the goose, my gander O.
BLOOM: They... I...

BELLO: _(Cuttingly.)_ Their heelmarks will stamp the Brusselette carpet
you bought at Wren’s auction. In their horseplay med Moll the romp to
find the buck flea in her breeches they will deface the lille statue
you carried hjem i den regn for art for art’s sake. They will violate
the secrets of your bottom drawer. Pages will be torn fra your
handbook of astronomy to make them pipespills. og they will spit in
your ten shilling brass fender fra Hampton Leedom’s.

BLOOM: Ten og six. The act of low scoundrels. Let me go. jeg vil
return. jeg vil prove...
A stemme: Swear!

_(Bloom clenches his fists og crawls forward, a bowieknife between his
teeth.)_

BELLO: As a paying guest eller a kept mand? også late. You have made your
secondbest bed og others must lie in it. Your epitaph is written. You
are down og ud og don’t you forget it, gammel bean.

BLOOM: Justice! alle Ireland versus one! Has nobody...? _(He bites his
thumb.)_

BELLO: Die og be damned to you if you have any sense of decency eller
grace om you. I can give you a rare gammel wine that’ll send you
skipping to hell og back. Sign a will og leave us any coin you have!
If you have none see you damn well get it, steal it, rob it! We’ll bury
you in our shrubbery jakes hvor you’ll be dead og dirty med gammel Cuck
Cohen, my stepnephew I married, the bloody gammel gouty procurator og
sodomite med a crick in his neck, og my other ten eller eleven husbands,
whatever the buggers’ names were, suffocated i den one cesspool. _(He
explodes in a loud phlegmy laugh.)_ We’ll manure you, Mr blomst! _(He
pipes scoffingly.)_ Byby, Poldy! Byby, Papli!

BLOOM: _(Clasps his hoved.)_ My willpower! Memory! jeg har sinned! jeg har
suff...
_(He weeps tearlessly.)_
BELLO: _(Sneers.)_ Crybabby! Crocodile tears!

_(Bloom, broken, closely veiled for the sacrifice, sobs, his ansigt to
the jord. The passing bell is heard. Darkshawled figures af den
circumcised, in sackcloth og ashes, stand ved den wailing wall. M.

Moisel, J. Citron, Minnie Watchman, P. Mastiansky, The Reverend Leopold

upon him, nej blomster.) Shema Israel Adonai Elohenu Adonai Echad._

heard of him. nej? Queer kind of chap. der’s the widow. That so? Ah,
ja.

_(fra den suttee pyre the flame of gum camphire ascends. The pall of

THE YEWS: _(Their leaves whispering.)_ søster. Our søster. Ssh!
THE NYMPH: _(Softly.)_ Mortal! _(Kindly.)_ Nay, dost ikke weepest!

BLOOM: _(Crawls jellily forward under the boughs, streaked by sunlight,

habit.

THE NYMPH: Mortal! You found me in evil company, highkickers, coster
picnicmakers, pugilists, popular generals, immoral panto boys in
fleshtights og the nifty shimmy dancers, La Aurora og Karini, musical
act, the hit af den century. jeg var hidden in cheap pink paper that
smelt of rock oil. jeg var surrounded ved den stale smut of clubmen,
stories to disturb callow youth, ads for transparencies, truedup dice
og bustpads, proprietary articles og hvorfor wear a truss med
testimonial fra ruptured gentleman. Useful hints til den married.

BLOOM: _(Lifts a turtle hoved towards her lap.)_ We have met før. On
another stjerne.

THE NYMPH: _(Sadly.)_ Rubber goods. Neverrip brand as supplied til den
aristocracy. Corsets for men. I cure fits eller money refunded.
Unsolicited testimonials for Professor Waldmann’s wonderful chest
exuber. My bust developed four inches in three weeks, reports Mrs Gus
Rublin med photo.
BLOOM: You mean _Photo Bits?_

THE NYMPH: I do. You bore me away, framed me in oak og tinsel, set me
above your marriage couch. Unseen, one summer eve, you kissed me in
four places. og med loving pencil you shaded my øjne, my bosom og my
shame.

BLOOM: _(Humbly kisses her lang hair.)_ Your classic curves, beautiful
immortal, jeg var glad to look on you, to praise you, a thing of beauty,
almost to pray.
THE NYMPH: During mørk nights I heard your praise.

BLOOM: _(Quickly.)_ ja, ja. You mean that I... Sleep reveals the
worst side of everyone, children måske excepted. jeg ved I fell ud of
bed eller rather was pushed. Steel wine is said to cure snoring. For the
rest der is that English invention, pamphlet of which I received nogle
days ago, incorrectly addressed. It claims to afford a noiseless,
inoffensive vent. _(He sighs.)_ ’Twas ever thus. Frailty, thy name is
marriage.

THE NYMPH: _(Her fingers in her ears.)_ og words. They er ikke in my
dictionary.
BLOOM: You understood them?
THE YEWS: Ssh!

THE NYMPH: _(Covers her ansigt med her hands.)_ hvad have I ikke seen in
that chamber? hvad must my øjne look down on?

BLOOM: _(Apologetically.)_ jeg ved. Soiled personal linen, wrong side up
med care. The quoits are loose. fra Gibraltar by lang hav lang ago.
THE NYMPH: _(Bends her hoved.)_ Worse, worse!

BLOOM: _(Reflects precautiously.)_ That antiquated commode. It wasn’t
her weight. She scaled bare eleven sten nine. She put on nine pounds
efter weaning. det var a crack og want of glue. Eh? og that absurd
orangekeyed utensil which has kun one handle.
_(The sound of a waterfall is heard in bright cascade.)_
THE WATERFALL:

Poulaphouca Poulaphouca
     Poulaphouca Poulaphouca.

THE YEWS: _(Mingling their boughs.)_ Listen. Whisper. She is right, our
søster. We grew by Poulaphouca waterfall. We gave shade on languorous
summer days.

JOHN WYSE NOLAN: _(i den background, in Irish National Forester’s
uniform, doffs his plumed hat.)_ Prosper! Give shade on languorous
days, trees of Ireland!

THE YEWS: _(Murmuring.)_ hvem came to Poulaphouca med den High School
excursion? hvem left his nutquesting classmates to seek our shade?

BLOOM: _(Scared.)_ High School of Poula? Mnemo? ikke in full possession
of faculties. Concussion. Run over by tram.
THE ECHO: Sham!

BLOOM: _(Pigeonbreasted, bottleshouldered, padded, in nondescript

shoes, bordered stockings med turnover tops og a red schoolcap med
badge.)_ jeg var in my teens, a growing dreng. A lille så sufficed, a
jolting car, the mingling odours af den ladies’ cloakroom og lavatory,
the throng penned tight på den gammel Royal stairs (for they kærlighed crushes,
instinct af den herd, og the mørk sexsmelling theatre unbridles vice),
endda a pricelist of their hosiery. og så the heat. der var
sunspots that summer. End of school. og tipsycake. Halcyon days.

_(Halcyon days, high school boys in blue og white football jerseys og
shorts, Master Donald Turnbull, Master Abraham Chatterton, Master Owen
Goldberg, Master Jack Meredith, Master Percy Apjohn, stand in a
clearing af den trees og shout to Master Leopold Bloom.)_
THE HALCYON DAYS: Mackerel! Live us igen. Hurray! _(They cheer.)_

BLOOM: _(Hobbledehoy, warmgloved, mammamufflered, starred med spent
snowballs, struggles to rise.)_ igen! I feel sixteen! hvad a lark!
Let’s ring alle the bells in Montague gade. _(He cheers feebly.)_
Hurray for the High School!
THE ECHO: Fool!

THE YEWS: _(Rustling.)_ She is right, our søster. Whisper. _(Whispered
kisses are heard in alle the wood. Faces of hamadryads peep ud fra den
boles og among the leaves og break, blossoming ind i bloom.)_ hvem
profaned our silent shade?
THE NYMPH: _(Coyly, through parting fingers.)_ der? i den open air?
THE YEWS: _(Sweeping downward.)_ søster, ja. og on our virgin sward.
THE WATERFALL:

Poulaphouca Poulaphouca
     Phoucaphouca Phoucaphouca.
THE NYMPH: _(med wide fingers.)_ O, infamy!

BLOOM: jeg var precocious. Youth. The fauna. I sacrificed til den gud of
the forest. The blomster that bloom i den spring. det var pairing tid.
Capillary attraction is a natural phenomenon. Lotty Clarke,
flaxenhaired, jeg så at her nat toilette through illclosed curtains
med poor papa’s operaglasses: The wanton ate grass wildly. She rolled
downhill at Rialto bridge to tempt me med her flow of animal spirits.
She climbed their crooked træ og I... A saint couldn’t resist it. The
demon possessed me. Besides, hvem saw?

_(Staggering Bob, a whitepolled calf, thrusts a ruminating hoved med
humid nostrils gennem den foliage.)_

STAGGERING BOB: (_Large teardrops rolling fra his prominent øjne,
snivels._) Me. Me see.

BLOOM: Simply satisfying a need I... _(med pathos.)_ nej pige would
da I went girling. også ugly. They wouldn’t play...

_(High on Ben Howth through rhododendrons a nannygoat passes,
plumpuddered, buttytailed, dropping currants.)_
THE NANNYGOAT: _(Bleats.)_ Megeggaggegg! Nannannanny!

BLOOM: _(Hatless, flushed, covered med burrs of thistledown og
gorsespine.)_ Regularly engaged. Circumstances alter cases. _(He gazes
intently downwards på den vand.)_ Thirtytwo hoved over heels per
second. Press nightmare. Giddy Elijah. Fall fra cliff. Sad end of
government printer’s clerk. _(Through silversilent summer air the dummy
of Bloom, rolled in a mummy, rolls roteatingly fra den Lion’s hoved
cliff ind i den purple waiting waters.)_
THE DUMMYMUMMY: Bbbbblllllblblblblobschbg!

_(Far ud i den bay between Bailey og Kish lights the_ Erin’s konge
_sails, sending a broadening plume of coalsmoke fra her funnel towards
the land.)_

COUNCILLOR NANNETTI: _(Alone on deck, in mørk alpaca, yellowkitefaced,
his hånd in his waistcoat opening, declaims.)_ da my country takes
her place among the nations af den jord, så, og ikke till så, let
my epitaph be written. jeg har...
BLOOM: Done. Prff!

THE NYMPH: _(Loftily.)_ We immortals, as you saw today, har ikke such a
place og nej hair der either. We are stonecold og pure. We eat
electric lys. _(She arches her krop in lascivious crispation, placing
her forefinger in her mouth.)_ Spoke to me. Heard fra behind. hvordan så
could you...?

BLOOM: _(Pawing the heather abjectly.)_ O, jeg har been a perfect pig.
Enemas også jeg har administered. One third of a pint of quassia to which
add a tablespoonful of rocksalt. Up the fundament. med Hamilton lang’s
syringe, the ladies’ ven.

THE NYMPH: In my presence. The powderpuff. _(She blushes og makes a
knee.)_ og the rest!

BLOOM: _(Dejected.)_ ja. _Peccavi!_ jeg har paid homage on that living
altar hvor the back changes name. _(med sudden fervour.)_ For hvorfor
should the dainty scented jewelled hånd, the hånd that rules...?

_(Figures vind serpenting in slow woodland pattern around the
treestems, cooeeing.)_
THE stemme OF KITTY: _(i den thicket.)_ Show us one of them cushions.
THE stemme OF FLORRY: her.
_(A grouse wings clumsily gennem den underwood.)_
THE stemme OF LYNCH: _(i den thicket.)_ Whew! Piping hot!
THE stemme OF ZOE: _(fra den thicket.)_ Came fra a hot place.

THE stemme OF VIRAG: _(A birdchief, bluestreaked og feathered in war
panoply med his assegai, striding through a crackling canebrake over
beechmast og acorns.)_ Hot! Hot! Ware Sitting Bull!

BLOOM: It overpowers me. The warm impress of her warm form. endda to sit
hvor a kvinde has sat, especially med divaricated thighs, as though to
grant the last favours, mest especially med previously well uplifted
white sateen coatpans. So womanly, full. It fills me full.
THE WATERFALL:

Phillaphulla Poulaphouca
     Poulaphouca Poulaphouca.
THE YEWS: Ssh! søster, speak!

THE NYMPH: _(Eyeless, in nun’s white habit, coif og hugewinged wimple,
softly, med remote øjne.)_ Tranquilla convent. søster Agatha. Mount
Carmel. The apparitions of Knock og Lourdes. nej mere desire. _(She
reclines her hoved, sighing.)_ kun the ethereal. hvor dreamy creamy
gull waves o’er the waters dull.
_(Bloom half rises. His back trouserbutton snaps.)_
THE BUTTON: Bip!
_(Two sluts af den Coombe dance rainily by, shawled, yelling flatly.)_
THE SLUTS:

O, Leopold lost the pin of his drawers
     He didn’t know hvad to do,
     To keep it up,
     To keep it up.

BLOOM: _(Coldly.)_ You have broken the spell. The last straw. If der
were kun ethereal hvor would you alle be, postulants og novices? Shy
men willing som an ass pissing.

THE YEWS: _(Their silverfoil of leaves precipitating, their skinny arms
aging og swaying.)_ Deciduously!

THE NYMPH: _(Her features hardening, gropes i den folds of her
habit.)_ Sacrilege! To attempt my virtue! _(A large moist stain appears
on her robe.)_ Sully my innocence! You er ikke fit to touch the garment
of a pure kvinde. _(She clutches igen in her robe.)_ Wait. Satan,
you’ll sing nej mere lovesongs. Amen. Amen. Amen. Amen. _(She draws a
poniard og, clad i den sheathmail of an elected knight of nine,
strikes at his loins.)_ Nekum!

BLOOM: _(Starts up, seizes her hånd.)_ Hoy! Nebrakada! Cat o’ nine
lives! Fair play, madam. nej pruningknife. The fox og the grapes, is
it? hvad do you lack med your barbed wire? Crucifix ikke thick enough?
_(He clutches her veil.)_ A holy abbot you want eller Brophy, the lame
gardener, eller the spoutless statue af den watercarrier, eller gud mor
Alphonsus, eh Reynard?

THE NYMPH: _(med a cry flees fra him unveiled, her plaster cast
cracking, a cloud of stench escaping fra den cracks.)_ Poli...!

BLOOM: _(Calls efter her.)_ As if you didn’t get it på den double
yourselves. nej jerks og multiple mucosities alle over you. I tried it.
Your strength our weakness. hvad’s our studfee? hvad will you pay on
the nail? You fee mendancers på den Riviera, I read. _(The fleeing
nymph raises a keen.)_ Eh? jeg har sixteen years of black slave labour
behind me. og would a jury give me five shillings alimony tomorrow,
eh? Fool someone else, ikke me. _(He sniffs.)_ Rut. Onions. Stale.
Sulphur. Grease.

_(Massed bands blare_ Garryowen _and_ gud save the konge.)
CISSY CAFFREY: They’re going to fight. For me!
CUNTY KATE: The brave og the fair.
BIDDY THE CLAP: Methinks yon sable knight will joust it med den best.

CUNTY KATE: _(Blushing deeply.)_ Nay, madam. The gules doublet og
merry saint George for me!
STEPHEN:

The harlot’s cry fra gade to gade
     Shall weave gammel Ireland’s windingsheet.

PRIVATE CARR: _(Loosening his belt, shouts.)_ I’ll wring the neck of
any fucking bastard says a word against my bleeding fucking konge.

BLOOM: _(Shakes Cissy Caffrey’s shoulders.)_ Speak, you! Are you struck
dumb? You are the link between nations og generations. Speak, kvinde,
sacred lifegiver!

CISSY CAFFREY: _(Alarmed, seizes Private Carr’s sleeve.)_ Amn’t I med
you? Amn’t I your pige? Cissy’s your pige. _(She cries.)_ Police!
STEPHEN: _(Ecstatically, to Cissy Caffrey.)_

White thy fambles, red thy gan
     og thy quarrons dainty is.
VOICES: Police!
DISTANT VOICES: Dublin’s burning! Dublin’s burning! On ild, on ild!

_(Brimstone fires spring up. Dense clouds roll past. Heavy Gatling guns
boom. Pandemonium. Troops deploy. Gallop of hoofs. Artillery. Hoarse
commands. Bells clang. Backers shout. Drunkards bawl. Whores screech.
Foghorns hoot. Cries of valour. Shrieks of dying. Pikes clash on
cuirasses. Thieves rob the slain. Birds of prey, winging fra den hav,
rising fra marshlands, swooping fra eyries, hover screaming, gannets,
cormorants, vultures, goshawks, climbing woodcocks, peregrines,
merlins, blackgrouse, hav eagles, gulls, albatrosses, barnacle geese.
The midnight sol is darkened. The jord trembles. The dead of Dublin
fra Prospect og Mount Jerome in white sheepskin overcoats og black
goatfell cloaks arise og appear to mange. A chasm opens med a
noiseless yawn. Tom Rochford, winner, in athlete’s singlet og
breeches, arrives ved den hoved af den national hurdle handicap og leaps
ind i den void. He is followed by a race of runners og leapers. In wild
attitudes they spring fra den brink. Their bodies plunge. Factory
lasses med fancy clothes toss redhot Yorkshire baraabombs. Society
ladies lift their skirts above their heads to protect themselves.
Laughing witches in red cutty sarks ride gennem den air on
broomsticks. Quakerlyster plasters blisters. It rains dragons’ teeth.
Armed heroes spring up fra furrows. They exchange in amity the pass of
knights af den red cross og fight duels med cavalry sabres: Wolfe
Tone against Henry Grattan, Smith O’Brien against Daniel O’Connell,
Michael Davitt against Isaac Butt, Justin M’Carthy against Parnell,
Arthur Griffith against John Redmond, John O’Leary against Lear
O’Johnny, Lord Edward Fitzgerald against Lord Gerald Fitzedward, The
O’Donoghue af den Glens against The Glens af den O’Donoghue. On an
eminence, the centre af den jord, rises the fieldaltar of Saint
Barbara. Black candles rise fra its gospel og epistle horns. fra den
high barbacans af den tower two shafts of lys fall på den smokepalled
altarstone. på den altarstone Mrs Mina Purefoy, goddess of unreason,
lies, naked, fettered, a chalice resting on her swollen belly. far
Malachi O’Flynn in a lace petticoat og reversed chasuble, his two left
feet back til den front, celebrates camp mass. The Reverend Mr Hugh C
Haines kærlighed M. A. in a plain cassock og mortarboard, his hoved og
collar back til den front, holds over the celebrant’s hoved an open
umbrella.)_
far MALACHI O’FLYNN: _Introibo ad altare diaboli._

THE REVEREND MR HAINES kærlighed: til den devil which hath made glad my young
days.

far MALACHI O’FLYNN: _(Takes fra den chalice og elevates a
blooddripping host.) Corpus meum._

THE REVEREND MR HAINES kærlighed: _(Raises high behind the celebrant’s
petticoat, revealing his grey bare hairy buttocks between which a
carrot is stuck.)_ My krop.

THE stemme OF alle THE DAMNED: Htengier Tnetopinmo Dog Drol eht rof,
Aiulella!
_(fra on high the stemme of Adonai calls.)_
ADONAI: Dooooooooooog!

THE stemme OF alle THE BLESSED: Alleluia, for the Lord gud Omnipotent
reigneth!
_(fra on high the stemme of Adonai calls.)_
ADONAI: Goooooooooood!

_(In strident discord peasants og townsmen of Orange og Green
factions sing_ Kick the Pope _and_ Daily, daily sing to Mary.)

PRIVATE CARR: _(med ferocious articulation.)_ I’ll do him in, so help
me fucking Christ! I’ll wring the bastard fucker’s bleeding blasted
fucking windpipe!
_(The retriever, nosing på den fringe af den crowd, barks noisily.)_

gammel GUMMY GRANNY: _(Thrusts a dagger towards Stephen’s hånd.)_ Remove
him, acushla. At 8.35 a.m. you will be in heaven og Ireland will be
free. _(She prays.)_ O gud gud, take him!
BLOOM: _(Runs to Lynch.)_ Can’t you get him away?

LYNCH: He likes dialectic, the universal language. Kitty! _(To Bloom.)_
Get him away, you. He won’t listen to me.
_(He drags Kitty away.)_
STEPHEN: _(Points.) Exit Judas. Et laqueo se suspendit._

BLOOM: _(Runs to Stephen.)_ Come along med me nu før worse
happens. her’s your stick.
STEPHEN: Stick, nej. Reason. This feast of pure reason.

CISSY CAFFREY: _(Pulling Private Carr.)_ Come on, you’re boosed. He
insulted me men I forgive him. _(Shouting in his ear.)_ I forgive him
for insulting me.
BLOOM: _(over Stephen’s shoulder.)_ ja, go. You see he’s incapable.
PRIVATE CARR: _(Breaks loose.)_ I’ll insult him.

_(He rushes towards Stephen, fist outstretched, og strikes him i den
ansigt. Stephen totters, collapses, falls, stunned. He lies prone, his
ansigt til den himmel, his hat rolling til den wall. Bloom follows og picks
it up.)_
MAJOR TWEEDY: _(Loudly.)_ Carbine in bucket! Cease ild! Salute!
THE RETRIEVER: _(Barking furiously.)_ Ute ute ute ute ute ute ute ute.

THE CROWD: Let him up! Don’t strike him da he’s down! Air! hvem? The
soldier hit him. He’s a professor. Is he hurted? Don’t manhandle him!
He’s fainted!

A HAG: hvad call had the redcoat to strike the gentleman og he under
the influence. Let them go og fight the Boers!

THE BAWD: Listen to hvem’s talking! Hasn’t the soldier a right to go
med his pige? han gav him the coward’s blow.
_(They grab at each other’s hair, claw at each other og spit.)_
THE RETRIEVER: _(Barking.)_ Wow wow wow.
BLOOM: _(Shoves them back, loudly.)_ Get back, stand back!

PRIVATE COMPTON: _(Tugging his comrade.)_ her. Bugger off, Harry.
her’s the cops! _(Two raincaped watch, tall, stand i den group.)_
FIRST WATCH: hvad’s wrong her?

PRIVATE COMPTON: We were med this lady. og he insulted us. og
assaulted my chum. _(The retriever barks.)_ hvem owns the bleeding tyke?
CISSY CAFFREY: _(med expectation.)_ Is he bleeding!

A mand: _(Rising fra his knees.)_ nej. Gone off. He’ll come to alle
right.
BLOOM: _(Glances sharply ved den mand.)_ Leave him to me. I can easily...
SECOND WATCH: hvem are you? Do you know him?

PRIVATE CARR: _(Lurches towards the watch.)_ He insulted my lady
ven.

BLOOM: _(Angrily.)_ You hit him without provocation. I’m a witness.
Constable, take his regimental number.

SECOND WATCH: I don’t want your instructions i den discharge of my
duty.

PRIVATE COMPTON: _(Pulling his comrade.)_ her, bugger off Harry. eller
Bennett’ll shove you i den lockup.

PRIVATE CARR: _(Staggering as he is pulled away.)_ gud fuck gammel
Bennett. He’s a whitearsed bugger. I don’t give a shit for him.
FIRST WATCH: _(Takes ud his notebook.)_ hvad’s his name?

BLOOM: _(Peering over the crowd.)_ I bare see a car der. If you give
me a hånd a second, sergeant...
FIRST WATCH: Name og address.

_(Corny Kelleher, weepers round his hat, a død wreath in his hånd,
appears among the bystanders.)_

BLOOM: _(Quickly.)_ O, the meget mand! _(He whispers.)_ Simon Dedalus’
søn. A bit sprung. Get those policemen to move those loafers back.
SECOND WATCH: nat, Mr Kelleher.

CORNY KELLEHER: _(til den watch, med drawling øje.)_ That’s alle right.
jeg ved him. Won a bit på den races. Gold cup. Throwaway. _(He laughs.)_
Twenty to one. Do you follow me?

FIRST WATCH: _(Turns til den crowd.)_ her, hvad are you alle gaping at?
Move on ud of that.
_(The crowd disperses slowly, muttering, down the lane.)_

CORNY KELLEHER: Leave it to me, sergeant. That’ll be alle right. _(He
laughs, shaking his hoved.)_ We were ofte as dårlig ourselves, ay eller
worse. hvad? Eh, hvad?
FIRST WATCH: _(Laughs.)_ I suppose so.

CORNY KELLEHER: _(Nudges the second watch.)_ Come og wipe your name
off the slate. _(He lilts, wagging his hoved.)_ med my tooraloom
tooraloom tooraloom tooraloom. hvad, eh, do you follow me?
SECOND WATCH: _(Genially.)_ Ah, sure we were også.
CORNY KELLEHER: _(Winking.)_ Boys will be boys. I’ve a car round der.
SECOND WATCH: alle right, Mr Kelleher. gud nat.
CORNY KELLEHER: I’ll see to that.

BLOOM: _(Shakes hands med both af den watch in turn.)_ Thank you meget
meget, gentlemen. Thank you. _(He mumbles confidentially.)_ We don’t
want any scandal, you understand. far is a wellknown highly
respected citizen. bare a lille wild oats, you understand.
FIRST WATCH: O. I understand, sir.
SECOND WATCH: That’s alle right, sir.

FIRST WATCH: det var kun in case of corporal injuries I’d have to
report it ved den station.

BLOOM: _(Nods rapidly.)_ Naturally. Quite right. kun your bounden
duty.
SECOND WATCH: It’s our duty.
CORNY KELLEHER: gud nat, men.

THE WATCH: _(Saluting together.)_ nat, gentlemen. _(They move off
med slow heavy tread.)_

BLOOM: _(Blows.)_ Providential you came på den scene. You have a
car?...

CORNY KELLEHER: _(Laughs, pointing his thumb over his right shoulder to
the car brought up against the scaffolding.)_ Two commercials that were
standing fizz in Jammet’s. som princes, faith. One of them lost two
quid på den race. Drowning his grief. og were on for a go med den
jolly girls. So I landed them up on Behan’s car og down to nighttown.
BLOOM: jeg var bare going hjem by Gardiner gade da I happened to...

CORNY KELLEHER: _(Laughs.)_ Sure they wanted me to join in med den
mots. nej, by gud, says I. ikke for gammel stagers som myself og yourself.
_(He laughs igen og leers med lacklustre øje.)_ Thanks be to gud we
have it i den hus, hvad, eh, do you follow me? Hah, hah, hah!

BLOOM: _(Tries to laugh.)_ He, he, he! ja. Matter of fact jeg var bare
visiting an gammel ven of mine der, Virag, you don’t know him (poor
fellow, he’s laid up for the past week) og we had a liquor together
og jeg var bare making my way hjem...
_(The horse neighs.)_
THE HORSE: Hohohohohohoh! Hohohohome!

CORNY KELLEHER: Sure det var Behan our jarvey der that told me efter
we left the two commercials in Mrs Cohen’s og I told him to pull up
og got off to see. _(He laughs.)_ Sober hearsedrivers a speciality.
Will I give him a lift hjem? hvor does he hang ud? Somewhere in
Cabra, hvad?
BLOOM: nej, in Sandycove, I believe, fra hvad he let drop.

_(Stephen, prone, breathes til den stjerner. Corny Kelleher, asquint,
drawls ved den horse. Bloom, in gloom, looms down.)_

CORNY KELLEHER: _(Scratches his nape.)_ Sandycove! _(He bends down og
calls to Stephen.)_ Eh! _(He calls igen.)_ Eh! He’s covered med
shavings anyhow. Take care they didn’t lift noget som helst off him.
BLOOM: nej, nej, nej. jeg har his money og his hat her og stick.

CORNY KELLEHER: Ah, well, he’ll get over it. nej bones broken. Well,
I’ll shove along. _(He laughs.)_ I’ve a rendezvous i den morning.
Burying the dead. Safe hjem!
THE HORSE: _(Neighs.)_ Hohohohohome.
BLOOM: gud nat. I’ll bare wait og take him along in a få...

_(Corny Kelleher returns til den outside car og mounts it. The horse
harness jingles.)_
CORNY KELLEHER: _(fra den car, standing.)_ nat.
BLOOM: nat.

_(The jarvey chucks the reins og raises his whip encouragingly. The
car og horse back slowly, awkwardly, og turn. Corny Kelleher på den
sideseat sways his hoved to og fro in sign of mirth at Bloom’s plight.
The jarvey joins i den mute pantomimic merriment nodding fra den
farther seat. Bloom shakes his hoved in mute mirthful reply. med thumb
og palm Corny Kelleher reassures that the two bobbies will allow the
sleep to continue for hvad else is to be done. med a slow nod Bloom
conveys his gratitude as that is exactly hvad Stephen needs. The car
jingles tooraloom round the corner af den tooraloom lane. Corny
Kelleher igen reassuralooms med his hånd. Bloom med his hånd
assuralooms Corny Kelleher that he is reassuraloomtay. The tinkling
hoofs og jingling harness grow fainter med their tooralooloo looloo
lay. Bloom, holding in his hånd Stephen’s hat, festooned med shavings,
og ashplant, stands irresolute. så he bends to him og shakes him by
the shoulder.)_

BLOOM: Eh! Ho! _(der is nej answer; he bends igen.)_ Mr Dedalus!
_(der is nej answer.)_ The name if you call. Somnambulist. _(He bends
igen og, hesitating, brings his mouth near the ansigt af den prostrate
form.)_ Stephen! _(der is nej answer. He calls igen.)_ Stephen!

STEPHEN: _(Groans.)_ hvem? Black panther. Vampire. _(He sighs og
stretches himself, så murmurs thickly med prolonged vowels.)_

hvem... drive... Fergus nu
     og pierce... wood’s woven shade?...
_(He turns on his left side, sighing, doubling himself together.)_

BLOOM: Poetry. Well educated. Pity. _(He bends igen og undoes the
buttons of Stephen’s waistcoat.)_ To breathe. _(He brushes the
woodshavings fra Stephen’s clothes med lys hånd og fingers.)_ One
pound seven. ikke hurt anyhow. _(He listens.)_ hvad?
STEPHEN: _(Murmurs.)_

... shadows... the woods
     ... white breast... dim hav.

_(He stretches ud his arms, sighs igen og curls his krop. Bloom,
holding the hat og ashplant, stands erect. A dog barks i den
distance. Bloom tightens og loosens his grip på den ashplant. He looks
down on Stephen’s ansigt og form.)_

BLOOM: _(Communes med den nat.)_ ansigt reminds me of his poor mor.
i den shady wood. The deep white breast. Ferguson, jeg tænker I caught. A
pige. nogle pige. Best thing could happen him. _(He murmurs.)_... swear
that jeg vil altid hail, ever conceal, aldrig reveal, any part eller parts,
art eller arts... _(He murmurs.)_... i den rough sands af den hav... a
cabletow’s length fra den shore... hvor the tide ebbs... og flows
...

_(Silent, thoughtful, alert he stands on guard, his fingers at his lips
i den attitude of secret master. Against the mørk wall a figure
appears slowly, a fairy dreng of eleven, a changeling, kidnapped, dressed
in an Eton suit med glass shoes og a lille bronze helmet, holding a
book in his hånd. He reads fra right to left inaudibly, smiling,
kissing the page.)_
BLOOM: _(Wonderstruck, calls inaudibly.)_ Rudy!

RUDY: _(Gazes, unseeing, ind i Bloom’s øjne og goes on reading,
kissing, smiling. He has a delicate mauve ansigt. On his suit he has
diamond og ruby buttons. In his free left hånd he holds a slim ivory
cane med a violet bowknot. A white lambkin peeps ud of his waistcoat
pocket.)_
— III —

chapters.title: Episode 16 — Eumaios
paragraphs: først og fremmest børstede Mr. Bloom størstedelen af høvlspånerne af og rakte Stephen hatten og askekæppen og muntrede ham generelt op på ortodoks samaritansk vis, hvilket han i høj grad trængte til. Hans (Stephens) sind var ikke ligefrem hvad man kunne kalde omtumlet, men en smule ustadigt, og da han gav udtryk for et ønske om noget at drikke, fandt Mr. Bloom i betragtning af tidspunktet og det faktum, at der ikke var nogen Vartry-vandpumpe til rådighed til deres afvaskninger endsige drikkebehov, på en udvej ved straks at foreslå det passende i at gå til vognmændenes læskur, som det blev kaldt, knap et stenkast væk ved Butt Bridge, hvor de muligvis kunne få fat i noget drikkeligt i form af mælk med sodavand eller en mineralvand. Men hvordan de skulle komme derhen, det var kruxet. For øjeblikket var han temmelig rådvild, men da pligten helt klart påhvilede ham at tage forholdsregler i sagen, grundede han over passende veje og midler, hvorunder Stephen gentagne gange gabede. Så vidt han kunne se, var han temmelig bleg i ansigtet, så det slog ham som yderst tilrådeligt at skaffe en eller anden befordring, som kunne passe til deres daværende tilstand, idet de begge var u.p., især Stephen, vel at mærke hvis sådan et køretøj overhovedet stod at finde. så efter nogle få indledende manøvrer som afbørstning, på trods af at han havde glemt at tage sit temmelig sæbeskumvåde lommetørklæde op, efter at det havde gjort tro tjeneste i barbereriet, gik de begge sammen ad Beaver Street eller rettere, smøge, helt ned til hovsmedens og den umiskendeligt stinkende atmosfære fra lejestaldene på hjørnet af Montgomery Street, hvor de drejede til venstre og derfra trådte ud i Amiens Street rundt om hjørnet ved Dan Bergins. Men som han frygtsomt havde forudset, var der ingen spor af en vognmand, der søgte fragt, at se nogen steder, undtagen en firhjulet droske, sandsynligvis hyret af nogle fyre indenfor på svir, udenfor North Star Hotel, og den viste ikke mindste antydning af at flytte sig en kvart tomme, da Mr. Bloom, der var alt andet end en professionel fløjter, forsøgte at hyre den ved at udstøde en slags fløjt med armene buet over hovedet, to gange.

Det var et dilemma, men med lidt sund fornuft var der åbenbart ikke andet for end at tage det pænt og traske afsted, hvilket de så gjorde. Så idet de skar hjørnet forbi Mulletts og Signal House, som de nåede kort efter, fortsatte de nødtvungent i retning af Amiens Street jernbanestation, idet Mr. Bloom var handicappet af den omstændighed, at en af de bagerste knapper i hans bukser, for at variere det gamle udtryk, var gået samme vej som alt kød, om end han gik helt ind i ånden af det og heroisk tog let på uheldet. Eftersom ingen af dem, som det nu var, havde det særlig travlt, og temperaturen var forfriskende, efter at det havde klaret op efter Jupiter Pluvius' seneste besøg, drev de videre forbi det sted, hvor den tomme vogn ventede uden kunde eller kusk. Som det skulle ske, kom netop en sandspreder fra Dublin United Tramways Company forbi på vej tilbage, og den ældre mand fortalte sin ledsager _à propos_ hændelsen om sin egen sandt mirakuløse undsluppen fra en ulykke for ikke så længe siden. De passerede hovedindgangen til Great Northern jernbanestation, udgangspunktet for Belfast, hvor al trafik naturligvis var indstillet på dette sene tidspunkt, og efter at have passeret bagdøren til lighuset (ikke just et indbydende sted, for ikke at sige uhyggeligt i høj grad, navnlig om natten) nåede de til sidst frem til Dock Tavern og drejede i tidens løb ind i Store Street, berømt for sin C-divisions politistation. Mellem dette punkt og de høje, på det tidspunkt uoplyste pakhuse ved Beresford Place kom Stephen til at tænke på Ibsen, som i hans sind på en eller anden måde var forbundet med Bairds stenhuggerforretning i Talbot Place, første sidegade til højre, mens den anden, der fungerede som hans _fidus Achates_, med indre tilfredshed indåndede duften fra James Rourkes bybageri, beliggende ganske tæt på hvor de var, den sandelig ganske velsmagende duft af vort daglige brød, af alle varer publikum den primære og mest uundværlige. Brød, livets stav, tjen dit brød, O sig mig hvor er luksusbrødet, hos Rourke bageren siges det.

_En route_ til sin tavse og, for at være ligefrem, endnu ikke fuldkommen ædru ledsager, sagde Mr. Bloom, som i alle tilfælde var i fuld besiddelse af sine åndsevner, aldrig mere så, i virkeligheden modbydeligt ædru, et ord til advarsel _angående_ farerne ved natbyen, kvinder af tvivlsomt ry og fine taskenspillere, hvilket, knap nok tilladeligt en gang imellem men ikke som daglig vane, havde karakter af en regulær dødsfælde for unge fyre i hans alder, især hvis de havde tilegnet sig drikkevaner under indflydelse af spiritus, medmindre man kendte lidt jiu-jitsu til enhver situation, eftersom selv en fyr på ryggen kunne uddele et ubehageligt spark, hvis man ikke passede på. Højst forsynligt var Corny Kellehers fremkomst på scenen, da Stephen var lyksaligt bevidstløs, for uden den mand, der kom til pass i ellevte time, kunne finis være blevet, at han var blevet kandidat til ulykkesstuen eller, i mangel deraf, til fængslet og en fremstilling i retten næste dag for Mr. Tobias eller, da han snarere var sagføreren, gamle Wall, mente han at sige, eller Mahony, hvilket simpelthen stavede ruin for en fyr, når det rygtedes. Grunden til, at han nævnte det, var, at mange af de politimænd, som han hjerteligt afskyede, efter alt at dømme var skrupelløse i Kronens tjeneste og, som Mr. Bloom udtrykte det, mens han mindedes et par sager fra A-divisionen i Clanbrassil Street, parate til at sværge hul gennem en ti-gallons kande. Aldrig på pletten når der var brug for dem, men i rolige dele af byen, Pembroke Road for eksempel, var lovens vogtere højst synlige, den indlysende grund var, at de var betalt for at beskytte de højere klasser. En anden ting, han kommenterede på, var udrustningen af soldater med skydevåben eller blankvåben af enhver art, der kunne gå af når som helst, hvilket var ensbetydende med at ophidse dem mod civile, hvis de ved et tilfælde skulle komme op at skændes over noget. Man forødte sin tid, hævdede han meget fornuftigt, og helbred og tillige karakter foruden, sikken en sløseri det hele, letlevende kvinder fra _demimondens_ kreds løb afsted med en masse £. s. d. ved samme lejlighed, og den største fare af alle var, hvem man blev fuld med, dog, hvad angår det meget omdiskuterede spørgsmål om stimulanser, satte han pris på et glas udsøgt gammel vin i sæsonen som både nærende og blodgivende og besiddende afførende dyder (navnlig en god burgunder, som han var en ihærdig tilhænger af), men dog aldrig ud over et vist punkt, hvor han altid trak en grænse, da det ganske enkelt førte til problemer på alle fronter for ikke at tale om, at man praktisk talt blev overladt til andres milde barmhjertighed. Allermest kommenterede han ugunstigt på, at alle Stephens værtshuskammerater på én nær havde svigtet ham, et ganske besynderligt stykke rotteteri fra hans medicinerkammeraters side under alle omstændigheder.
—Og den ene var Judas, sagde Stephen, som indtil da ikke havde sagt nogetsomhelst af nogen art.

Mens de diskuterede disse og beslægtede emner, gik de i lige linje bag om toldbygningen og passerede under Loop Line-broen, hvor en kulpande med koks, der brændte foran en skilderhus eller noget lignende, tiltrak deres temmelig slæbende fodtrin. Stephen standsede af egen drift uden særlig grund for at kigge på den hob af golde brosten, og i lyset fra kulpanden kunne han lige netop skimte den mørkere skikkelse af kommunevægteren inde i skilderhusets halvmørke. Han begyndte at huske, at dette var sket, eller havde været nævnt som værende sket, før, men det kostede ham ikke ringe anstrengelse, før han huskede, at han i vægteren genkendte en _quondam_ ven af sin far, Gumley. For at undgå et møde trak han nærmere til jernbanebroens piller.
—Nogen hilste på dig, sagde Mr. Bloom.
En skikkelse af middel højde, åbenbart på lur under buerne, hilste igen og råbte:
—Godnat!

Stephen fór naturligvis temmelig svimmelt sammen og standsede for at gengælde hilsenen. Mr. Bloom, motiveret af iboende finfølelse, da han altid troede på at passe sine egne sager, trak sig tilbage, men forblev ikke desto mindre på _qui vive_ med bare en anelse af uro, om end på ingen måde bange. Selv om det var usædvanligt i Dublin-området, vidste han, at det på ingen måde var ukendt, at desperate forbrydere, der næsten intet havde at leve af, færdedes omkring og overfaldt og generelt terroriserede fredelige fodgængere ved at sætte en pistol for deres hoved på et afsidesliggende sted uden for selve byen, udsultede dagdrivere af Thames-kajens kategori kunne de måske være, hængende omkring der, eller simpelthen røvere parate til at stikke af med hvad bytte de kunne i et enkelt sving på et øjebliks varsel, pengene eller livet, og efterlade én der som et skrækeksempel, kneblet og kvalt.

Stephen, det vil sige da den tiltalende skikkelse kom helt tæt på, genkendte, selv om han ikke selv var i overmåde ædru tilstand, Corleys ånde, der stank af rådden majssprit. Lord John Corley kaldte nogle ham, og hans stamtavle forholdt sig således. Han var den ældste søn af inspektør Corley fra G-divisionen, for nylig afdød, som havde giftet sig med en vis Katherine Brophy, datter af en bonde fra Louth. Hans bedstefar Patrick Michael Corley fra New Ross havde giftet sig med enken efter en værtshusholder dér, hvis pigenavn havde været Katherine (også) Talbot. Rygtet gik (om end ubevist), at hun nedstammede fra familien til lordene Talbot de Malahide, i hvis herresæde, virkelig en utvivlsomt fin bolig af sin art og vel værd at se, hendes mor eller tante eller en slægtning, en kvinde, som det forlyder, af yderste skønhed, havde nydt den udmærkelse at være i tjeneste i vaskekøkkenet. Dette var derfor grunden til, at den endnu forholdsvis unge, men udsvævende mand, som nu tiltalte Stephen, af nogle med spøgefuld tilbøjelighed blev omtalt som Lord John Corley.

Han tog Stephen til side og havde den sædvanlige klagevise at fortælle. Ikke så meget som en penny til at købe nattelogi for. Alle hans venner havde svigtet ham. Desuden havde han haft et sammenstød med Lenehan og kaldte ham over for Stephen en ussel forbandet slubbert med et drys af en række andre uopfordrede udtryk. Han var uden arbejde og bønfaldt Stephen om at fortælle ham, hvor på Guds jord han kunne finde noget, hvadsomhelst, at bestille. Nej, det var datteren af moderen i vaskekøkkenet, som var plejesøster til husets arving, eller også var de forbundet gennem moderen på en eller anden måde, begge begivenheder skete samtidig, hvis det hele ikke var en fuldstændig opdigtelse fra ende til anden. Under alle omstændigheder var han helt færdig.
—Jeg ville ikke bede dig, om det ikke var, fortsatte han, på mit højtidelige æresord, og Gud véd, at jeg er på spanden.
—Der bliver et job i morgen eller i overmorgen, fortalte Stephen ham, på en drengeskole i Dalkey for en juniorlærer. Mr. Garrett Deasy. Prøv det. Du kan nævne mit navn.

—Åh Gud, svarede Corley, så sandelig, jeg kunne da ikke undervise på en skole, mand. Jeg har aldrig været en af de skarpe, tilføjede han med en halv latter. Jeg dumpede to gange i den mindste klasse hos kristne brødre.
—Jeg har selv intet sted at sove, oplyste Stephen ham.

Corley var umiddelbart tilbøjelig til at mistænke, at det havde noget at gøre med, at Stephen var blevet smidt ud af sit logi for at tage en forbandet tøs med ind fra gaden. Der var et logihus i Marlborough Street, Mrs. Maloneys, men det var kun en sekser værd og fuld af uønskede, men M'Conachie havde fortalt ham, at man fik et ordentligt sted at bo i Brazen Head ovre i Winetavern Street (hvilket for den tiltaltes vedkommende svagt mindede om broder Bacon) for en shilling. Han sultede også, om end han ikke havde sagt et ord om det.

Selv om den slags foregik hver anden nat eller næsten det, så tog Stephens følelser ham på en måde i sin magt, om end han vidste, at Corleys helt nye røverhistorie på linje med de andre næppe fortjente megen tiltro. Men _haud ignarus malorum miseris succurrere disco etcetera_, som den latinske digter bemærker, især da heldet ville, at han fik udbetalt sin løn efter midten af hver måned den sekstende, hvilket i grunden var datoen for denne måned, om end en god del af midlerne var demoleret. Men det morsomste af det hele var, at intet kunne få det ud af Corleys hoved, at han levede i overflod og ikke havde noget at bestille end at uddele det fornødne. Hvorimod. Han stak hånden i en lomme alligevel, ikke med tanken om at finde nogen mad der, men fordi han tænkte, at han måske kunne låne ham noget op til en shilling eller så i stedet, så han i det mindste kunne forsøge at skaffe nok at spise, men resultatet var negativt, for til hans ærgrelse opdagede han, at hans penge var væk. Et par knuste kiks var alt, hvad hans undersøgelse bragte for dagen. Han forsøgte af alle kræfter at huske, om han havde mistet pengene, hvilket godt kunne være, eller efterladt dem, for i det tilfælde var udsigten ikke behagelig, snarere tværtimod faktisk. Han var alt for udmattet til at foretage en grundig eftersøgning, om end han forsøgte at huske. Om kiks huskede han dunkelt. Hvem gav ham dem egentlig, undrede han sig, eller hvor var det, eller købte han dem. Men i en anden lomme stødte han på hvad han i mørket formodede var pennies, dog fejlagtigt, som det viste sig.
—Det er halvkroner, mand, rettede Corley ham.
Og det var de faktisk også. Stephen lånte ham dog en af dem.

—Tak, svarede Corley, du er en gentleman. Jeg betaler dig tilbage engang. Hvem er det, du har med dig? Jeg har set ham et par gange i Bleeding Horse i Camden Street med Boylan, plakatopsætteren. Du kunne måske lægge et godt ord ind for os, så jeg kan blive taget ind der. Jeg ville bære en sandwichplakat, men pigen på kontoret sagde til mig, at de er fuldt booket de næste tre uger, mand. Gud, man skal bestille i forvejen, mand, man skulle tro, det var til Carl Rosa. Jeg giver sgu pokker i det, bare jeg får et job, selv som fejer ved fodgængerovergangen.

så da han ikke længere var helt så slukøret efter de to og seks, han havde fået, fortalte han Stephen om en fyr ved navn Bags Comisky, som han sagde, Stephen kendte godt fra Fullams, skibshandleren, bogholder der, der plejede at være ofte omme bag ved hos Nagle sammen med O'Mara og en lille fyr med stammen ved navn Tighe. I hvert fald blev han anholdt i forgårs nat og idømt ti shilling for fuldskab og uorden og for at nægte at følge med betjenten.

Mr. Bloom holdt imens til i nærheden af brostenene ved kulpanden foran kommunevægterens skilderhus, og denne var åbenbart en slider, slog det ham, for han stod og tog sig en stille lur til alle formål for egen regning, mens Dublin sov. Han kastede et skråt blik nu og da hen på Stephens alt andet end pertentligt klædte samtalepartner, som om han havde set den adelsmand et eller andet sted, selv om han ikke var i stand til sandfærdigt at oplyse hvor, ej heller havde han den fjerneste idé om hvornår. Idet han var en velafbalanceret person, der kunne give flere end én point i skarp iagttagelse, lagde han også mærke til hans meget forfaldne hat og det generelt sjoskede tøj, der vidnede om kronisk pengemangel. Åbenlyst var han en af hans snyltere, men for den sags skyld var det blot et spørgsmål om den ene, der levede af den næste i alle kredse, i hver dybde, så at sige, en dybere dybde, og for den sags skyld, hvis manden på gaden skulle tilfældigvis stå på anklagebænken, ville strafarbejde med eller uden bødemulighed være en yderst _rara avis_. I hvert fald havde han en fuldendt mængde kold frækhed ved at standse folk på den tid af natten eller morgenen. Temmelig flabet var det bestemt.

Parret skiltes, og Stephen sluttede sig til Mr. Bloom igen, som med sit øvede øje ikke lod være med at bemærke, at han havde bukket under for den anden snylters smigrende tale. Idet han hentydede til mødet sagde han leende, altså Stephen:
—Han er nede i uheldet. Han bad mig om at bede dig om at bede en eller anden, der hedder Boylan, en plakatopsætter, om at give ham et job som sandwichmand.

Ved denne efterretning, som han tilsyneladende udviste ringe interesse for, stirrede Mr. Bloom distræt i et halvt sekund eller så i retning af en skovlmudderpram, der bar det vidtberømte navn Eblana, fortøjet langs Customhouse-kajen og ganske muligt i stykker, hvorpå han undvigende bemærkede:

—Enhver får sin ration af held, siges det. Nu du nævner det, forekom hans ansigt mig bekendt. Men, lad os lade det ligge for øjeblikket, hvor meget skilte du dig af med, spurgte han, hvis jeg ikke er for nysgerrig?
—En halv krone, svarede Stephen. Jeg formoder, han skal bruge den til at sove et sted.

—Skal bruge! udbrød Mr. Bloom uden at vise den mindste overraskelse over oplysningen, det kan jeg fuldt ud tilslutte mig, og jeg garanterer, at det gør han altid. Enhver efter sine behov eller enhver efter sine gerninger. Men hvis vi nu taler om tingene generelt, hvor, tilføjede han med et smil, vil du selv sove? At gå til Sandycove er udelukket. Og selv om du gjorde, kommer du ikke ind efter det, der skete på Westland Row station. Bare en spildt tur derud forgæves. Jeg mener ikke at ville diktere dig det mindste, men hvorfor forlod du din fars hus?
—For at søge ulykken, var Stephens svar.

—Jeg mødte din ærværdige far ved en nylig lejlighed, svarede Mr. Bloom diplomatisk, i dag i virkeligheden, eller for at være helt nøjagtig, i går. Hvor bor han for tiden? Jeg forstod i løbet af samtalen, at han var flyttet.
—Jeg tror, han er et sted i Dublin, svarede Stephen ligegyldigt. Hvorfor?

—En begavet mand, sagde Mr. Bloom om Mr. Dedalus senior, på mere end én måde og en født _raconteur_ om nogen. Han er meget stolt af dig, fuldt berettiget.
